findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback. Unlike disconnectMutation (lines 61-64) it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, and in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper onChanged is props.onChanged which may be undefined. After a successful deletion the cached query still contains the old cacheUpdatedAt, so the dropdown continues to show 'Cache Status / Delete cached data' as if the cache still exists until a manual refetch/remount.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache entries that will never be served
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering expiresAt. getCachedAvailability treats rows with expiresAt < now as a cache miss, so connectedCalendars can report cacheUpdatedAt and the UI can offer 'Delete cached data' for a cache that is already expired/dead. The status query should only consider unexpired rows (expiresAt >= now), matching the read path.

findings.title: Authorization failure is thrown as a generic Error instead of a TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential does not belong to the session user the handler throws `new Error('Credential not found or access denied')`. In tRPC this surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN client error, so clients and monitoring treat a routine bad/foreign credentialId as a server failure. Throw a TRPCError with an appropriate code instead, as other viewer handlers do.

findings.title: sed invocation is macOS-only and the script exits 0 on failure
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU/Linux sed treats '' as an input file and fails, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated while the script continues and prints success. Additionally the failure paths at lines 49 and 58 call cleanup(), which unconditionally `exit 0`, masking rate-limit and tunnel-start failures. Use a portable in-place edit (or OS detection) and exit non-zero on the error paths.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on unpinned npx-fetched tsx that is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency, line 196) to `npx tsx`, but tsx is not declared anywhere in this package's dependencies. Running dev:cron therefore requires a network fetch of an unpinned package on first use, fails offline/in locked-down installs, and is a supply-chain/reproducibility regression unrelated to the calendar-cache feature. Add tsx as a devDependency (pinned by the lockfile) or keep ts-node.
